summary: Powles Head light at the eastern entrance to Trepassey Harbour, Newfoundland: buoys first, light lit 1902, combined light and fog building since 1960; grounds open, tower closed.

light.fog_signal: horn, 4 s blast every 60 s (diaphone from 1907; electronic from 1972)
light.note: Coast Guard list (dated 2026-09-24): Fl W 10s, flash 0.2 s and eclipse 9.8 s; fog horn blast 4 s, silence 56 s. Rowlett: white light, 1 s on and 9 s off, focal plane 31 m. The 1902 light (Lighthouse Friends): one-second periods of light and darkness from a fifth-order lens at 31 m. The 1925 replacement kept the same signature (Lighthouse Friends).

structures.note: Painted white; joined to the wooden keeper's dwelling by a 9.1 m passageway (Lighthouse Friends). Replaced in 1925.
Painted white (Lighthouse Friends; nllh3d). Replaced in 1960 after rusting.

structures.type: cylindrical, red and white, on the combined light and fog-alarm building
structures.note: Coast Guard list: red and white cylindrical tower, 2.4 m. Rowlett: 9 m (30 ft) square cylindrical tower with lantern and gallery, rising from one corner of a square one-storey fog-signal building; Rowlett notes that the Coast Guard lists 2.4 m. Lighthouse Friends: a square tower rising from one corner of the 1960 combination building. The height and shape differ between sources; the record uses the Coast Guard figure.

Two keepers' dwellings built near the new light in 1961 (Lighthouse Friends). Lighthouse Friends says the assistant keeper's dwelling was removed after 1990; the Newfoundland 3D gallery says the keeper's dwelling was removed in 1990.

staffing.note: Disputed. Lighthouse Friends says the station became a one-person post in 1990 and 'is no longer staffed'; the Newfoundland 3D gallery says it became unmanned in 1990 when the keeper's dwelling was removed. The Fisheries and Oceans brochure (page modified 2019-09-24) lists Powles Head among the staffed lightstations; the station record's 2010 Coast Guard list also names it staffed.

access.note: Set from the record's staffed status, which is disputed. Grounds open, tower closed (Lighthouse Friends; Rowlett). Gravel road of about 5 km from Trepassey, walking or four-wheel drive recommended (Rowlett); Lighthouse Friends describes the last 4 km as dirt road.

events.note: Captain John Orlebar proposes a light on Powles Head to guide ships into Trepassey Harbour; Robert Oke, Superintendent of Lighthouses, drew the plans (Lighthouse Friends).
Courtenay automatic whistling buoy anchored off Powles Head in June. Adrift in September; recovered, moored again, then lost and destroyed (Lighthouse Friends).
Buoy placed in 1882 dragged ashore by ice in February 1883; buoy removed from service in winter from then on (Lighthouse Friends).
On 4 December 1890 the buoy was torn from its moorings and went ashore near Cape Mutton. Men who recovered it would not return it until paid $80 (Lighthouse Friends). No cause given.
Buoy lost after going adrift again. Inspector Richard White visits, chooses Powles Head over Pounder Cove; a cast-iron tower and a Champion foghorn in storage (Lighthouse Friends).
Light first exhibited; square wooden tower, fifth-order lens, one second light and one second dark, focal plane 31 m (Lighthouse Friends). Rowlett: station established 1902.
John Devereux hired as first keeper, with J. Waddleton as assistant (Lighthouse Friends).
Gun-cotton fog alarm replaced by a diaphone: five-second blasts, 112 seconds of silence (Lighthouse Friends).
Wooden tower replaced by a round iron tower, painted white, same signature (Lighthouse Friends; nllh3d).
Rusted iron tower replaced by the present combination light and fog-alarm building with a square tower (Lighthouse Friends; nllh3d; Rowlett gives 1960).
Two keepers' dwellings built near the new light (Lighthouse Friends).
Commercial power reached the station (Lighthouse Friends; nllh3d).
Diaphone fog signal changed to an electronic signal (Lighthouse Friends).

Station becomes a one-person post; the assistant keeper's dwelling is removed (Lighthouse Friends). The Newfoundland 3D gallery says the keeper's dwelling was removed in 1990, making the station unmanned.

corrections.proposed: unknown: unmanned since 1990 per Lighthouse Friends and the Newfoundland 3D gallery; staffed per the 2010 Coast Guard list and the 2019 DFO brochure
corrections.why: The record calls the station staffed. Two sources say it has been unmanned since the 1990 removal of a keeper's dwelling; two (the 2010 list and the 2019 DFO brochure) name it staffed. The record should show the dispute, and a human should check the current status before any page says 'staffed'.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Lighthouse Friends and the Newfoundland 3D gallery: unmanned from 1990. DFO brochure (2019): staffed. The 2010 list in the record: staffed. Rowlett (undated): a 1961 keeper's house 'occupied by a keeper'. Not settled. The story gives each account.

Coast Guard list: red and white cylindrical tower, 2.4 m. Rowlett: 9 m square cylindrical tower on a one-storey fog-signal building, and notes the Coast Guard figure. Lighthouse Friends: square tower on the 1960 combination building. The record uses the Coast Guard figure.

Coast Guard list: Fl W 10s. Rowlett: 1 s on, 9 s off, consistent with the Coast Guard list. The 1902 light (Lighthouse Friends) was one second on and one second off; its later characteristic changes are not dated.
Coast Guard list: blast 4 s, silence 56 s. Lighthouse Friends: diaphone from 1907 with 5 s blasts and 112 s silence. Rowlett: a blast every 30 s. Dates of changes after 1907 are not given.

Lighthouse Friends: the assistant keeper's dwelling was removed after the station became a one-person post. Newfoundland 3D gallery: the keeper's dwelling was removed in 1990. Both agree on the year; they name different dwellings. The story reports both wordings.

notes_for_editor: The history is almost all Lighthouse Friends, which cites the Journal of the House of Assembly of Newfoundland and the Canadian Coast Guard's Newfoundland light lists; none of those was read. The Newfoundland 3D gallery's text overlaps with Lighthouse Friends and was used only for the 1990 unmanned status, the 1925 and 1960 changes and the 1863 proposal. Staffing is the unresolved point: the station record's 'staffed (as of 2010)' rests on the April 2010 Coast Guard list, which the 2011 Senate report 'Seeing the Light' reprints; that report was not read for this station. The DFO brochure (2019) also names it staffed; Lighthouse Friends and the 3D gallery say it has been unmanned since 1990. A human should check the current status with the Coast Guard before any page says 'staffed'. Keeper names: John Devereux, J. Waddleton and Tom Corrigan are as Lighthouse Friends spells them; no years are given, so none is invented. Tom Corrigan is named only in his public role as last keeper. The Canadian Marine annual reports in the corpus name no Powles Head light; the only Trepassey item is a 1902 tide gauge. A Chronicling America search for 'Powles Head' returned only unrelated personal names. Facebook group posts, Tripadvisor and the 1000 Towns and Whoa Dana web pages were seen in search and not used. The federal heritage designations CSV does not list the station. Wikipedia not used. Fact-check (2026-10-28): the story's 'Trepassey road' detail is now attributed to Lighthouse Friends (6.7 km from Route 10, last 4 km dirt) and Rowlett (5 km gravel, walking or 4WD recommended), not merged. The 1990 dwelling removal is worded as 'later' (Lighthouse Friends: 'subsequently'), not 'that year'. Footnote 3 now names the Powles Head entry, not a Placentia heading; the Rowlett entry sits in the Cape Race area of that page. The 1972 electronic signal is cited to Lighthouse Friends only; the 1925 'same signature' to Lighthouse Friends only.
